verdicts.reviewer_notes: Fourth review. All five review-3 required changes are applied verbatim: the new summary first sentences, and key obligations 1, 2, 4 and 5. I re-fetched the leginfo bill text, the bill status page and Cal. Const. art. IV sec. 8. Confirmed against the bill text: frontier model means trained above 10^26 integer or floating-point operations (22757.11). A large frontier developer has more than $500M in annual gross revenues together with affiliates. 22757.12(a) puts the framework duty on large frontier developers. Annual review and the 30-day publication of material modifications are in 22757.12(b). The transparency report duty in 22757.12(c)(1) reads verbatim 'a frontier developer shall ... publish ... a transparency report' 'Before, or concurrently with, deploying'. Under 22757.12(d), a large frontier developer sends OES internal-use summaries 'every three months or pursuant to another reasonable schedule'. Under 22757.13, 'A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident ... to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days'. Labor Code 1107.1(a) anti-retaliation applies to 'A frontier developer', and 1107.1(e)(1) puts the anonymous process on 'A large frontier developer'. CalCompute is 'operative only upon an appropriation in a budget act'. The status page shows approval on 29 Sep 2025, Chapter 138, and no urgency clause. Art. IV sec. 8(c)(1) still supports the 1 January 2026 in_force date. Both timeline URLs are primary (leginfo). A grep of content/ found SB 53 only under content/runs/, so it is not a duplicate. Tone is neutral. Reading the remaining obligations against the verbatim text turned up two inaccuracies, so claim_matches_source fails. (1) Key obligation 3 says 'Report critical safety incidents to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days (24 hours if imminent danger)'. The 15-day report goes to OES. The 24-hour disclosure under 22757.13 does not: the text says the developer 'shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction, that is appropriate based on the nature of that incident'. Its trigger is 'an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury', not 'imminent danger'. As worded, the obligation implies the 24-hour notice goes to OES. (2) Key obligation 6 says 'Civil penalties up to $1 million per violation, enforced by the Attorney General' without saying who is liable. Sec. 22757.15(a) reads verbatim 'A large frontier developer that fails to publish or transmit a compliant document ..., makes a statement in violation of subdivision (e) of Section 22757.12, fails to report an incident as required by Section 22757.13, or fails to comply with its own frontier AI framework shall be subject to a civil penalty ... that does not exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000) per violation'. The revised summary now says all frontier developers carry duties. So the unscoped penalty line implies that non-large frontier developers face the $1M penalty, and the statute does not say that. Sec. 22757.15(b) confirms that only the Attorney General can bring the civil action. Earlier reviews missed both issues. No other problems found. The summary needs no change beyond these two obligations.
required_changes: Change key obligation 3 to: 'Frontier developers: report critical safety incidents to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovery; if an incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority (e.g. law enforcement or a public safety agency)'.

Change key obligation 6 to: 'Large frontier developers: civil penalties up to $1 million per violation (e.g. failing to publish or transmit required documents, failing to report an incident, or not complying with their own framework), recoverable only in a civil action by the Attorney General'.
